dispositions.note: Resolved by narrowing the wording, the second option I offered. Rule 10 ('Append-only; no improvement without new evidence') now states what check_history enforces: a better ledger status needs a relied-on digest no earlier ledger holds, and each claim whose verdict improves, matched by claim ID, needs such a digest among that claim's checks; a successor may get worse. It calls this a floor, not retry control, and names the shapes it lets through: another check's changed outcome on unchanged evidence (my Y09, Y10), a renamed or dropped claim (Y06, Y07), and a policy violation no longer listed (Y11). It leaves the legitimacy of a re-run to H16's run lock, campaign records and no-retry-into-a-pass rule. 'Not claimed' adds that retry control is not claimed. Re-running my round-4 history probes on this commit gives the same results as round 4, and every result now matches the README. The superseded wording 'the ledger refuses re-judging identical evidence' is gone.

Rule 10 and 'Not claimed' now say keeping one history per subject is H16's, and a ledger presented as the first of a second history for the same subject is a fork that only H16's records can show. My fork probe is still accepted by check_history, as the README now says.
